All reviewer edits were uncommitted and reverted; crates/ is byte-clean at the reviewed sha. | f-9c41 | defect | MAJOR | CRITICAL — a selective scope over a corpus larger than the expansion ceiling now FAILS the search where the old query answered it. The old candidate_vectors CTE applied the full admission EXISTS inside its WHERE, so ORDER BY &lt;=&gt; LIMIT $14 bounded the ADMITTED page and candidate_count counted admitted rows. The rewrite bounds the RAW page first (embeddings.rs:505-513) and admits afterwards (admitted_candidates, :584-589), so candidate_count (:515-517) now counts raw vectors scanned. The expansion loop's early exit is `hit_count &gt;= filters.limit \|\| scanned &lt; candidate_limit` (:749). While the corpus is larger than the page, scanned == candidate_limit on EVERY pass, so the early exit can never fire; the loop runs all nine passes (40 -&gt; 10,240 for limit=10, INITIAL_CANDIDATE_MULTIPLIER=4, CANDIDATE_GROWTH_FACTOR=2, MAX_CANDIDATE_EXPANSIONS=8) and then raises candidate_limit_exhausted (:767-768). This is the shape production is in — a small repo, a path glob, or a conversation pin inside a large shared index — and it is the exact geometry crates/daemon/tests/search_scope_starvation.rs was written to defend ('a repository holding a small share of a central index can therefore have every candidate deleted by its own anchor and be answered with silence'). The old code survived it because the anchor predicates were inside the CTE where hnsw.iterative_scan = strict_order could keep pulling batches; after the move, iterative_scan has almost nothing left to filter and the recovery burden falls entirely on the bounded Rust loop. It is also a user-visible OUTAGE rather than a short answer: fs3_store::search_elements' error propagates through crates/daemon/src/search.rs:341-345 via map_err(fail), which contradicts the design the same file states at :576-580 — 'failing it now over a diagnostic query would turn a working empty result into an outage'. Smallest fix: make the sentinel reflect ADMISSION exhaustion rather than raw-page fullness — carry count(*) FROM admitted_candidates (or an index-exhausted signal) alongside candidate_count and stop expanding when the admitted set stops growing; failing that, return the short page instead of Err at the bound, which is what the old query did. Restoring only the anchor predicates (repo/path/worktree/conversation) inside candidate_vectors while leaving the expensive smart_content resolution outside would also fix it and keep the O(candidates) win. | crates/store/src/embeddings.rs:505-517,584-589,717-771; crates/daemon/src/search.rs:341-345,576-580; crates/daemon/tests/search_scope_starvation.rs:1-22 | [x] checked | — | — | — | [goals](../../plan.dd.md#goals), [architecture](../../impl-guide.dd.md#architecture) | Paired probe, one fixture, only the SQL swapped. Fixture: 12,000 foreign vectors nearer the query than 5 in-scope vectors (ceiling for limit=10 is 10,240), repo-scoped search, limit 10. SHIPPED: 'REVIEWER_PROBE: Err(store query failed: encountered unexpected or invalid data: semantic search could not fill 10 distinct elements after 8 candidate expansions)'. OLD (SEARCH_ELEMENTS_SQL replaced by the pre-change statement recovered verbatim from origin/main): 'REVIEWER_PROBE: Ok with 5 hits: [Some("git:github.com/fixtures/scoped") x5]'. Independent SQL confirmation on fs3_review013_hunt1 (:5434) under the shipped session GUCs (hnsw.iterative_scan=strict_order, jit=off, max_parallel_workers_per_gather=0), sweeping the exact expansion sequence: NEW returns hits=0 with scanned==candidate_limit at every one of 40/80/160/320/640/1280/2560/5120/10240; OLD returns hits=5 scanned=5 at every step, i.e. it exits on pass 1. Cost of the failing path, EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) per pass summed: NEW 9 passes = 199.7 ms / 246,496 shared blocks then ERROR; OLD 1 pass = 29.33 ms / 24,576 shared blocks and a correct answer. Probe was appended to crates/store/tests/search_admission.rs, run, and reverted; git status shows crates/ clean. |
